titleStmt.title: The American Chargé at Tangier (Childs) to the French Resident General in Morocco (Puaux)

div.head: The American Chargé at Tangier (Childs) to the French Resident General in Morocco (Puaux)
div.p: Mr. Resident General: I have the honor to inform Your Excellency that the Legation is authorized to notify the Protectorate Government that the wartime restrictions which have been introduced into French Morocco as a result of joint action by the American and French authorities in North Africa are recognized as applicable to American ressortissants with the understanding that they are wartime measures which are applicable only for the duration of the present emergency, such recognition being withdrawable at the discretion of the Department of State, and is not to be interpreted as in any way prejudicing American treaty rights in Morocco or as in the nature of a precedent.

Consequently the application of the existing measures under reference to American ressortissants is subject to the specific reservations set forth in the Legation’s note to Your Excellency of April [February] 11, 1944 concerning the requisition of olive and wheat crops. Decision in all cases of dispute in the premises between American ressortissants and the local executive authorities shall appertain to the American consular authorities in French Morocco.

Every measure taken in the future as a result of joint action by the American and French authorities in North Africa of which the extension is intended to apply to Morocco will be the subject of a relative notification to Your Excellency in respect of the application of such measure to American nationals and protected persons.

In conclusion, Your Excellency may be assured of the fullest cooperation on the part of the Legation as well as of that of the American Consulates in the French Zone with the Protectorate authorities in an endeavor to promote the fulfilment of the purposes of the exceptional and temporary measures in question.

note.p: In despatch 2262, August 5, the Chargé transmitted a note of July 25 from the Resident General, which acknowledged receipt of this note of June 28 (881.044/7–1244).
